deep.reconstruction:
This page is a laboratory record from the Gauss–Weber electromagnetic induction work at Göttingen (bundle 'PH.Induktion'). It mentions Moritz Meyerstein, the Göttingen instrument maker who built apparatus for Gauss and Weber. The page has two unrelated blocks.

(A) Comparison table headed 'Wegmesser | Meyerstein'. 'Wegmesser' means path-meter, i.e. a measuring wheel or counter that records a length. The paired readings (Wegmesser value w_i, Meyerstein value m_i) are:
(9.9, 10), (19.9, 20), (29.9, 30), (39.9, 40), (429.9, 440), (919.9, 1040), (1318.9, 1440), (1620.9, 1740), (1828.0, 1940), (3055.0, 3163), (6475.9, 6686), (6739.9, 6976).
The last Wegmesser entry is overwritten; it reads 6739.9 in the image.
Below the table is the subtraction '− 2.4 wurden später wieder abgewickelt' ('2.4 were later unwound again'), giving 6739.9 − 2.4 = 6737.5.
The word 'abgewickelt' (unwound) strongly suggests that the table records wire being wound onto a coil (an induction multiplier or inductor). One count comes from the path-meter and the other from Meyerstein's own tally. The corrected total wound length on the meter scale is 6737.5 units.
The differences m_i − w_i are 0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 10.1, 120.1, 121.1, 119.1, 112.0, 108.0, 210.1, 236.1. They are not proportional to w_i, so there is no constant calibration factor. The two columns probably differ by miscounts, slippage, or different reference points rather than by a unit conversion. This is my interpretation; the page itself draws no conclusion.

(B) An observation series headed by the clock time 12h 57' 21''. Five pairs of scale readings, of the same kind as the magnetometer scale-division readings on the following page, are each replaced by their arithmetic mean:
- (614.9 + 614.8)/2 = 614.85
- (241.6 + 239.8)/2 = 240.70
- (611.7 + 613.8)/2 = 612.75
- (240.0 + 227.5)/2 = 233.75
- (621.9 + 603.9)/2 = 612.90
The means alternate between about 613 and about 237. This is the kind of alternation produced by repeated induction impulses that throw a magnetometer needle back and forth, as in Weber's multiplication or 'Zurückwerfung' method. The next page continues with pairwise sums and differences of the same kind.
If the reading is right, the amplitude being sought is about half the difference between the alternating means: (612.8 − 237.2)/2 ≈ 188 scale divisions. This last step is my inference; it is not written on the page.
errors: No arithmetic errors. All five means are exact, and 6739.9 − 2.4 = 6737.5.
The last Wegmesser entry was written over (an earlier digit is corrected). The corrected value 6739.9 is consistent with the subtraction.
